BABITA's DEATH SENTENCE

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
One year after Whistleblower Babita Deokaran was gunned down, we retrace her steps in the days leading up to her murder and reveal the unbelievable level of graft she uncovered.

Unique Selling Point:
- A POWERFUL STORY OF A WOMAN WHO’S INTEGRITY COST HER, HER LIFE.
- A FASCINATING LOOK AT THE FRAUD AND CORRUPTION THAT IS CRIPPLING OUR ECONOMY
- REMARKABLE INVESTIGATIVE JOURNALISM BY JEFF WICKS – PEOPLE WILL BE SHOCKED AT WHAT HE HAS PIECED TOGETHER.


Summary:
Babita Deokaran was a corruption whistle-blower within the Gauteng Department of Health. She was assassinated in a hit-style killing outside her south Johannesburg home in August 2021.

Babita stood no chance. She put her life on the line when she chose to speak out and expose deep rooted corruption within the Gauteng Dept of Health. She knew it would be dangerous - but doing the right thing ended up costing her – her life.

As a country we praise the whistleblowers as the pillars of truth and justice - Babita’s story is one that should shock and outrage the country – we cannot allow this failure of justice to be swept under rug.

The Babita story has not been told in detail, the shocking elements that reveal a complete disregard for whistleblowers safety has never been more evident. I think her family would be open to speaking now and it could make for a compelling story retracing her steps in the days leading up to her murder. The masterminds behind her hit are still walking free and the orchestrators of the graft are still in their position and drawing salaries paid for by us tax payers!

NEWS24 has done a remarkable 6 month long investigation – titled Silenced. We tell the story visually – the content is compelling and our reach will take the research to another level.


Further information:
WHO WAS BABITA DEOKARAN
A 53 year old accountant and senior manager at the Gauteng Health Department. As the chief director: financial accounting, Deokaran had a front row seat to fraud and corruption – she wasn’t someone to just sit and watch – she took action. Owing to her position, she was also in control of the evidentiary paper trail left by those who preyed on public funds, making her an invaluable asset to the Special Investigating Unit. She had been a lynchpin witness for the SIU and had cooperated with investigations spanning a decade.

THE HITMEN
Six alleged hitmen accused of executing the attack on Deokaran were arrested in the days after the killing and are standing trial for her murder.

If the state's case proves true, the men were tasked by an unknown paymaster with Deokaran's murder and were paid R400 000. The police investigation into her death remains open, as the supposed mastermind remains free.

WHAT BABITA UNCOVERED
 DUBIOUS SPENDING AT TEMBISA HOSPITAL - hospital management embarked on a buying spree, outstripping other larger central academic hospitals like Steve Biko in Pretoria and Charlotte Maxeke in Johannesburg. Collectively, this is nearly triple the amount of purchase orders for the nine largest hospitals in Gauteng combined.
 Flagged R850 million in possibly fraudulent transactions by a single hospital, with no open and transparent tender process through in just four months between April and July 2021. 1 203 purchase orders - valued between R400 000 and R500 000.
 She tried to stop R100 million in dodgy payments.

4 AUGUST 2021 – BABIT’S FIRST FLAG AT TEMBISA
Exactly 19 days before her murder, Deokaran filed a report that flagged "possible fraudulent transactions" in a payment run for that week. Of the R166 million earmarked to pay thousands of suppliers to the province’s hospitals and clinics, R104 million was needed to pay those of Tembisa Hospital alone.
By the time her surface-level investigation was complete and multiple payment schedules examined, she had identified R344 million bound for the hospital’s suppliers - exactly a quarter of the provincial department's R1.4 billion spend. She also provided a list of more than 217 companies she felt needed closer scrutiny.
In four months, Tembisa Hospital processed 1 232 purchase orders, each valued at less than R500 000. In total, this amounted to just over R600 million. Collectively, this is nearly triple the amount of purchase orders for the nine other hospitals combined.
 BABITA flagged payments from Tembisa Hospital to ANC Ekurhuleni leader Sello Sekhokho. He had three companies - even a security firm - supplying medical equipment at vastly inflated prices. Health department CFO Lerato Madyo instructed Deokaran to pay Sekhokho - and told her to keep it secret.

WHO DID SHE TELL & WHAT DID THEY DO?
 Twelve days before Babita was murdered, Gauteng Health CFO Lerato Madyo told the whistleblower that her report on dubious spending patterns at Tembisa Hospital had been escalated for an investigation.
• This never happened, and, to date, nearly R850m in payments from the hospital to little-known suppliers has yet to be probed. The first time Madyo spoke up about Deokaran's concerns was the day of her killing.

TEMBISA HOSPITAL ABUSING THE SYSTEM - RED FLAG 1.
The number of purchase orders out of the hospital, combined with their amounts under the threshold of R500 000 - is a red flag for fraud. It points to the practice of "split invoicing", regarded by forensic investigators and auditors as a strategy to avoid an open procurement process. The hospital exploited a loophole in public procurement legislation.
As Deokaran worked backward examining Tembisa Hospital's acquisitions, the scale of the bonanza was drawn into focus. Goods or services above that threshold require a public tender process….Below that mark, the hospital’s CEO can sign off.

STANDOUT DODGY DEALINGS
SUSPECT: Gauteng ANC heavyweight - Ekurhuleni leader Sello Sekhokho
ALLEGATION: He had three companies – an events company and even a security firm - supplying medical equipment at vastly inflated prices. The contracts he scored for providing medical supplies and equipment to Tembisa Hospital was worth R2.3 million
THE TRIGGER: His windfall flagged as "potentially fraudulent" by Babita just three weeks before she was murdered.
THE COMPANIES: Kaizen Projects (events) - Sekhokho is also the sole director of two other companies - Nokokhokho and Bollanoto Security.
Only Nokokhokho has an official website.The others have no online presence, and all operate from the same nondescript house in Isekelo Section, Tembisa, according to Companies and Intellectual Properties Commission data.nIn fact, the companies operate from a home office in Edenvale.
FINDINGS: In single weekly pay run, Kaizen, Nokokhokho and Bollanoto Security were due to be paid just shy of R1.5 million.
PRICE COMPARISON: The purchase of headblocks, his price was 533% above a fair market rate.

THE IMPACT OF HER DEATH?
It appears that once she was out of the way, little was done to further her inquiry.
Since her murder, only a random audit was undertaken. It did not focus on companies she suspected of extracting millions from the Tembisa Hospital but rather a random sample from all department procurement.

WHAT HAS THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH DONE? (NEWS24)
 The Department of Health revealed that her calls for a forensic investigation were cast aside. Instead, a compliance audit was undertaken. According to spokesperson Motalatale Modiba, the internal team "performed random audits across facilities". The findings, he said, identified weaknesses in supply chain management systems and controls, which were being addressed.
 In Tembisa, CEO Ashley Mthunzi claimed to have appointed a bid adjudication committee and a section that monitored demands for goods and services.

WHAT NEWS24 UNCOVERED
 Drawing from a trove of more than 60 000 emails and the contents of her cellphone – the details of her final graft probe has been revealed. The investigation has been running for 6 months.

 BABITA’s BOSS LIED TO HER ABOUT ESCALTING THE INVESTIGATION
Gauteng Health boss Lerato Madyo lied when she told Babita Deokaran that her discovery of R850m in dubious Tembisa Hospital payments had been bumped up the chain of command.
"There was never a report and request for an investigation…," then acting Gauteng Health HOD Sibongile Zungu said this week. "Ms Madyo did not communicate any request for an investigation prior to Ms Deokaran's passing," she added.
Madyo, as chief financial officer, is a central figure in Deokaran's final graft probe and was among the first to be notified that expenditure out of Tembisa Hospital was alarmingly high.
"Madyo did not communicate any request for an investigation… she did however share a screenshot of their Whatsapp conversation. [This was] not necessarily reporting or requesting an investigation but rather highlighting that it seemed like Babita had a premonition about the activities at Tembisa Hospital," Zungu added.

 LINKED DODGY COMPANIES
The hospital channeled nearly R60 million in payments to letterbox companies that exist only on paper. Twenty entities which simultaneously billed the hospital are controlled by four people - Samendran Chin, Sydney Thindelo, Kelvin Sills and Meshan Govender.
• Each registered five companies on the same day and provided fake addresses when doing so (CIPC data)
• The businesses sport obscure names. None have official websites. None are registered with the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (Sahpra), a prerequisite for trading in medical goods.
• Between May and June in 2021, 129 contracts were awarded to companies controlled by the four, at a rate of nearly three per day, according to Gauteng health department data in possession of News24.
**NEWS24 – broke down the contracts awarded to each person and the values – 05 AUG 2021.

 LINKED ANC EKHURULENI LEADER SELLO SEKHOKHO’s COMPANIES

 IDENTIFIED STAND OUT COUPLE THAT COINED R30 million
A part-time call centre agent and her sound engineer husband - Christine and Avikash Signarian - landed Tembisa Hospital contracts worth nearly R30 million (70 payments) in the space of a month - each control five companies that saw a flurry of trade from the hospital, contracted to provide everything from ventilators to ICU beds. News24 could not locate a single office or warehouse. None have official websites or social media pages. All correspondence was routed through Yahoo and Gmail addresses.
 PAYMENTS CONTINUED SINCE HER DEATH
Sources within the department told News24 that the payments continued – despite Babita’s damning report that she paid for with her own life.

 INDENTIFIED 30 companies that were trading without licenses and it is understood that Sahpra has assembled a task team to investigate.

INTERVIEWS
 JEFF WICKS – investigative journalist
 DEOKARAN FAMILY
EXPERT OPTIONS
 ALEX VAN DEN HEEVER - Chair of Social Security Systems Administration and Management Studies at Wits.
 OUTA – gov promises to eradicate corruption were lip service.
 SOUTH AFRICAN NATIONAL CIVI ORGANISATION - they have actively been pointing fingers at the ANC for funnelling contacts to their cronies.

 RIGHT OF REPLIES
o BABITA’s BOSS - Gauteng Department of Health CFO Lerato Madyo –
o TEMBISA CEO Ashley Mthunzi –
o DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH - spokesperson Motalatale Modiba
POSSIBLY - Acting Gauteng Health HOD Sibongile Zungu – threw Babita’s boss under the bus
o SELLO SEKHOKHO – 3 companies linked to dodgy payments
o THE DODGY COMPANIES – ALL DID NOT REPLY TO NEWS24 – they really tried – calls, whatsapps, emails, visits to last known addresses, sent physical letters – but NOTHING.

Script:


STRUCTURE

VISUAL START RE-ENACMENT SCENE OF BABITA SHOOTING

VO: Nine shots in broad daylight. Babita Deokaran stood no chance. She red flagged procurement irregularities at the Gauteng Department of Health and within three weeks, she was murdered.

LINK: The risks for speaking out and exposing deep rooted corruption are clear, but when threats turn into actions, the consequences can be severe - because those that risk being exposed want whistle-blowers to be silenced.

VO: As the Chief Director for Finance at Gauteng Department of Health - Babita Deokaran was a critical witness in corruption investigations for more than a decade.

TONY: it is so fresh in our memories, the hurt and the pain that we felt then as a family. We feel still feel that now a year gone on.

VO: Three days after being gunned down - six hitmen were arrested.

But on the anniversary of her of death – as family, friends and civic justice organisations gathered to celebrate Babita Deokaran’s life – there are still many unanswered questions around her murder. Tony Haripersad is the family spokesperson.

TONY: She didn't tell us in detail what she was really involved in or what she really faced. You know, we saw that she was tense. She kept that away from us. Work had to be work. And family was family.

LINK: A year later we still don’t know who the paymasters were behind the hit, but retracing her last steps before her murder, you quickly realise there was there was 850 million reasons for Babita Deokaran to die.

VO: Three Weeks before Deokaran’s assassination she filed a report on Tembisa Hospital in Gauteng - flagging 1203 purchase orders, all coming in under R500 000. It totalled R850 million in possibly fraudulent transactions that were submitted in just four months.

JEFF: what it appears to be, on the face of it, is an extraction network. Money was flying out of that hospital at a rate of knots

VO: Over the last six months, a News24 Team, led by Investigative Journalist Jeff Wicks, waded through over 60 000 of Deokaran’s emails and cellphone data – getting a vivid view of the last month of her life.

JEFF: I've never worked on a project of this scale before. Everything from Google searches to who she was talking to. This was her final graft investigation.

VO: Twelve days before she was taken out, Deokaran sent the following message to her boss – Gauteng Health Department CFO – Lerato Madyo.

I am just worried that the guys in Tembisa are going to realise we are not releasing their payments…. Our lives could be in danger.

Madyo indicated the report was escalated to the Head of Department.

But that never happened.

MASA: So your evidence proves that the CFO lied?
JEFF: We questioned the then HOD and she categorically denies that Lerato Madyo ever formally escalated the report over Babita’s concerns about her safety. In fact, the first time she learnt about BABITA’s safety concerns was on the day of her death.

VO: Deokaran lived her last days, with a false sense of security.

TONY: it hurts us to know that our loved one. Died. Believing that there was safety and protection and something happening to. Take care of her.

VO: Madyo declined our request for an interview - she referred us to the Gauteng Department of Health that in turn replied in writing - stating, they are finalising the appointment of an independent forensic investigator; are taking internal steps to address the flagged issues and promised decisive action will be taken.

But this only comes now, a year later, in the wake of the News24 series.

Alex van den Heever is from Wits University’s School of Governance. He is clear there needs to be criminal consequences and a forensic investigation is not the answer.

ALEX: It's basically not a police investigation. Any reasonable supply chain management structure would pick this up. And that suggests that basically everybody within the system is either too scared or they are or they are complicit.

VO: Deokaran flagged 217 businesses before her investigation was brutally cut short. Picking up where she left off, Wicks scrutinised at least 45 of those, many are nothing more than paper companies, seemingly geared to extract money through government contracts.
TAKE A BEAT
The team covered thousands of kilometers across the province in search of these companies and possibly some answers.

JEFF: We've travelled to townships to upmarket areas where these businesses are supposedly located and we haven't been able to find a single office. If someone had only looked when she warned them, they would have found the same thing.

VO: We took a drive to one of these so-called companies in the small town of Nigel, south of Johannesburg.

JEFF: This is the supposed business address of one of the companies that billed millions of Rand through contracts from Tembisa Hospital.
MASA: This company billed millions of rands.
JEFF: That’s what they’d have us believe, I mean, if you look at the CIPC data, this address is active and in theory a company that sells and stocks, medical supplies should operate from here. But the reality is somewhat different.

VO: The company is Avigeez, and its director is Avikash Signarian - he controls five companies that scooped more than R17 million from just 39 separate transactions.

LINK: With due diligence seeming lacking in government procurement – paper-companies have successfully coined millions of rands only to have the so-called directors the conveniently disappear without a trace….

VO: We tried contacting Signarian, but he appears to have dropped off the radar…

UPSOUND CALLING SEQUENCE - Three calls - different angles

VO: And that’s the thing about paper companies, they disappear as quickly as they were formed.

JEFF: I'm at the point where I don't expect to find anything, but I think it's important for us to really see this through to the end and we've got no intention of stopping.

VO: Wicks has uncovered blatant, brazen graft at Tembisa Hospital with orders pushed through for anything from medical supplies to wingback leather chairs and even skinny jeans - although, government claims that, was a typo.

The payments get even more suspicious when you realise that the transactions flagged by Deokaran all came in under R500 000.

JEFF: And that's a red flag because any amount above that requires a much more rigorous procurement process. Below 500,000 rand is within the CEO's delegation of authority.

ALEX: Deokaran, sitting at a central level within the department, was able to pick this up. But somehow the hospital wasn't.

JEFF: It's very easy to pick up the patterns because you'll have one individual who's a director of five companies.//she could never have known that at the time because she didn't have the space and the opportunity to investigate further before she was murdered.
MASA: She was silenced.
JEFF: She's been silenced for a year. And it's only on the back of our reporting that something seems to be being done about this.

VO: Of the 217 companies flagged by Deokaran, Kaizen Projects was one of the first she identified.

It’s owned by Sello Sekhokho - he is the recently elected Treasurer General of the ANC in Ekurhuleni. Wicks discovered that he also owns two other companies Nokokhokho and Bollanoto Security & Projects - all three businesses supplied Tembisa Hospital at the same time.

VO: For the record, as it stands, Sekhokho is not a murder suspect an he insists there’s nothing dodgy about his companies, he’s been doing business with government departments for years and has no idea why his companies were flagged.

MASA: None of your purchase orders exceed 500,000 rand. Some may call that suspicious. Is that a coincidence?
SELLO: It's up to supply chain in the institution to either reject or go with us. I can't see because of his less than five HUNDRED. Then maybe there's a suspicion that I was doing wrong things.

VO: Sekhokho claims he’s just like any other person submitting quotes and doesn’t know either the provincial CFO Lerato Madyo or the hospital CEO Dr. Ashley Mthunzi.

MASA: You're the treasurer general of the ANC in Ukhuruleni - that comes with power, it comes with influence and it comes with connections.
SELLO: I dispute the fact that a person is connected because he's the TREAURY of the ANC.
MASA: Really?
SELLO: No, it doesn't come with power.
MASA: It doesn't come with influence.
SELLO: No
MASA: It doesn’t come with connections.
SELLO: No, It does come with responsibility. That I'm given by the ANC comrades or ANC members in Ekurhuleni.

VO: But against the backdrop of state capture, it’s hard to accept that answer.

MASA: We were told that it's just a coincidence that all of his contracts don't exceed 500,000 Rands.
ALEX: Yeah, it's not a coincidence. I mean, statistically, that's not what would happen. /The first and foremost is why is the hospital permitting them?. M8

VO: Questionable pricing is also an instant red flag.

Sekhokho’s quoted R3900 for a single head block and R2106 for a cervical collar.

A quick costing exercise revealed shocking pricing discrepancies on these paramedical supplies.

A head block goes for R814.20, while a top of the range cervical collar is R147.80 . We put our findings to Sekhokho.

SELLO: No, you see, you are an asset. Next time I do an invoice, I mean, I do a quote I say to you, I need one, two, three. Can you get it for me? We are not getting these products. And if I'm not getting this product, what must we do? We have not overcharged.
MASA: You have!
SELLO: NO, we haven't.

VO: Interestingly, Tembisa Hospital CEO Dr. Ashley Mthunzi signed off on most of the suspicious invoices.

MASA: Can the TEMBIsA hospital, CEO perhaps claim ignorance?
JEFF: That would be equally as damaging for him because this expenditure, according to our evidence, happened under his watch. So at best he's incompetent and at worst he's culpable.

VO: While Dr. Mthunzi declined an interview, he was suspended alongside provincial CFO Lerato Madyo last week as the Special Investigation Unit moves forward with the case.

A move that’s long overdue.

JEFF: BABITA Deokaran did everything right// She picked up an anomaly. She reported it and she expected that something would be done. In fact, nothing was done and she was murdered. And that's the great tragedy of this story.

VO: Seeing wrongdoing and looking the other way was never in Babita Deokaran’s nature.

TONY: She died doing her job with integrity and diligently. She stood for the truth. And she would not Compromise. Our entire lives. Have been shaken and changed. We’ll never be the Same again. Because she is no more. So whilst we are. Paying the price as a family, the mastermind out there is still at large.

VO: Arresting the alleged hitmen, is simply not good enough.

ALEX: Another five can be hired for the next whistle blower. The end game for these hospitals in this investigation is that the key public sector people, people in public office responsible for this network, need to go to jail.

VO: But that would be up to the authorities.

JEFF: At the end of the day, we're journalists. We come into information, we verify it and we publish it. We're not the SIU or the police? And we're just making sure that everything that had been kept in the shadows is now in the light.




END

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 12 September 2022 Script: STRUCTURE VISUAL START RE-ENACMENT SCENE OF BABITA SHOOTING VO: Nine shots in broad daylight. Babita Deokaran stood no chance. She red flagged procurement irregularities at the Gauteng Department of Health and within three weeks, she was murdered. LINK: The risks for speaking out and exposing deep rooted corruption are clear, but when threats turn into actions, the consequences can be severe - because those that risk being exposed want whistle-blowers to be silenced. VO: As the Chief Director for Finance at Gauteng Department of Health - Babita Deokaran was a critical witness in corruption investigations for more than a decade. TONY: it is so fresh in our memories, the hurt and the pain that we felt then as a family. We feel still feel that now a year gone on. VO: Three days after being gunned down - six hitmen were arrested. But on the anniversary of her of death – as family, friends and civic justice organisations gathered to celebrate Babita Deokaran’s life – there are still many unanswered questions around her murder. Tony Haripersad is the family spokesperson. TONY: She didn't tell us in detail what she was really involved in or what she really faced. You know, we saw that she was tense. She kept that away from us. Work had to be work. And family was family. LINK: A year later we still don’t know who the paymasters were behind the hit, but retracing her last steps before her murder, you quickly realise there was there was 850 million reasons for Babita Deokaran to die. VO: Three Weeks before Deokaran’s assassination she filed a report on Tembisa Hospital in Gauteng - flagging 1203 purchase orders, all coming in under R500 000. It totalled R850 million in possibly fraudulent transactions that were submitted in just four months. JEFF: what it appears to be, on the face of it, is an extraction network. Money was flying out of that hospital at a rate of knots VO: Over the last six months, a News24 Team, led by Investigative Journalist Jeff Wicks, waded through over 60 000 of Deokaran’s emails and cellphone data – getting a vivid view of the last month of her life. JEFF: I've never worked on a project of this scale before. Everything from Google searches to who she was talking to. This was her final graft investigation. VO: Twelve days before she was taken out, Deokaran sent the following message to her boss – Gauteng Health Department CFO – Lerato Madyo. I am just worried that the guys in Tembisa are going to realise we are not releasing their payments…. Our lives could be in danger. Madyo indicated the report was escalated to the Head of Department. But that never happened. MASA: So your evidence proves that the CFO lied? JEFF: We questioned the then HOD and she categorically denies that Lerato Madyo ever formally escalated the report over Babita’s concerns about her safety. In fact, the first time she learnt about BABITA’s safety concerns was on the day of her death. VO: Deokaran lived her last days, with a false sense of security. TONY: it hurts us to know that our loved one. Died. Believing that there was safety and protection and something happening to. Take care of her. VO: Madyo declined our request for an interview - she referred us to the Gauteng Department of Health that in turn replied in writing - stating, they are finalising the appointment of an independent forensic investigator; are taking internal steps to address the flagged issues and promised decisive action will be taken. But this only comes now, a year later, in the wake of the News24 series. Alex van den Heever is from Wits University’s School of Governance. He is clear there needs to be criminal consequences and a forensic investigation is not the answer. ALEX: It's basically not a police investigation. Any reasonable supply chain management structure would pick this up. And that suggests that basically everybody within the system is either too scared or they are or they are complicit. VO: Deokaran flagged 217 businesses before her investigation was brutally cut short. Picking up where she left off, Wicks scrutinised at least 45 of those, many are nothing more than paper companies, seemingly geared to extract money through government contracts. TAKE A BEAT The team covered thousands of kilometers across the province in search of these companies and possibly some answers. JEFF: We've travelled to townships to upmarket areas where these businesses are supposedly located and we haven't been able to find a single office. If someone had only looked when she warned them, they would have found the same thing. VO: We took a drive to one of these so-called companies in the small town of Nigel, south of Johannesburg. JEFF: This is the supposed business address of one of the companies that billed millions of Rand through contracts from Tembisa Hospital. MASA: This company billed millions of rands. JEFF: That’s what they’d have us believe, I mean, if you look at the CIPC data, this address is active and in theory a company that sells and stocks, medical supplies should operate from here. But the reality is somewhat different. VO: The company is Avigeez, and its director is Avikash Signarian - he controls five companies that scooped more than R17 million from just 39 separate transactions. LINK: With due diligence seeming lacking in government procurement – paper-companies have successfully coined millions of rands only to have the so-called directors the conveniently disappear without a trace…. VO: We tried contacting Signarian, but he appears to have dropped off the radar… UPSOUND CALLING SEQUENCE - Three calls - different angles VO: And that’s the thing about paper companies, they disappear as quickly as they were formed. JEFF: I'm at the point where I don't expect to find anything, but I think it's important for us to really see this through to the end and we've got no intention of stopping. VO: Wicks has uncovered blatant, brazen graft at Tembisa Hospital with orders pushed through for anything from medical supplies to wingback leather chairs and even skinny jeans - although, government claims that, was a typo. The payments get even more suspicious when you realise that the transactions flagged by Deokaran all came in under R500 000. JEFF: And that's a red flag because any amount above that requires a much more rigorous procurement process. Below 500,000 rand is within the CEO's delegation of authority. ALEX: Deokaran, sitting at a central level within the department, was able to pick this up. But somehow the hospital wasn't. JEFF: It's very easy to pick up the patterns because you'll have one individual who's a director of five companies.//she could never have known that at the time because she didn't have the space and the opportunity to investigate further before she was murdered. MASA: She was silenced. JEFF: She's been silenced for a year. And it's only on the back of our reporting that something seems to be being done about this. VO: Of the 217 companies flagged by Deokaran, Kaizen Projects was one of the first she identified. It’s owned by Sello Sekhokho - he is the recently elected Treasurer General of the ANC in Ekurhuleni. Wicks discovered that he also owns two other companies Nokokhokho and Bollanoto Security & Projects - all three businesses supplied Tembisa Hospital at the same time. VO: For the record, as it stands, Sekhokho is not a murder suspect an he insists there’s nothing dodgy about his companies, he’s been doing business with government departments for years and has no idea why his companies were flagged. MASA: None of your purchase orders exceed 500,000 rand. Some may call that suspicious. Is that a coincidence? SELLO: It's up to supply chain in the institution to either reject or go with us. I can't see because of his less than five HUNDRED. Then maybe there's a suspicion that I was doing wrong things. VO: Sekhokho claims he’s just like any other person submitting quotes and doesn’t know either the provincial CFO Lerato Madyo or the hospital CEO Dr. Ashley Mthunzi. MASA: You're the treasurer general of the ANC in Ukhuruleni - that comes with power, it comes with influence and it comes with connections. SELLO: I dispute the fact that a person is connected because he's the TREAURY of the ANC. MASA: Really? SELLO: No, it doesn't come with power. MASA: It doesn't come with influence. SELLO: No MASA: It doesn’t come with connections. SELLO: No, It does come with responsibility. That I'm given by the ANC comrades or ANC members in Ekurhuleni. VO: But against the backdrop of state capture, it’s hard to accept that answer. MASA: We were told that it's just a coincidence that all of his contracts don't exceed 500,000 Rands. ALEX: Yeah, it's not a coincidence. I mean, statistically, that's not what would happen. /The first and foremost is why is the hospital permitting them?. M8 VO: Questionable pricing is also an instant red flag. Sekhokho’s quoted R3900 for a single head block and R2106 for a cervical collar. A quick costing exercise revealed shocking pricing discrepancies on these paramedical supplies. A head block goes for R814.20, while a top of the range cervical collar is R147.80 . We put our findings to Sekhokho. SELLO: No, you see, you are an asset. Next time I do an invoice, I mean, I do a quote I say to you, I need one, two, three. Can you get it for me? We are not getting these products. And if I'm not getting this product, what must we do? We have not overcharged. MASA: You have! SELLO: NO, we haven't. VO: Interestingly, Tembisa Hospital CEO Dr. Ashley Mthunzi signed off on most of the suspicious invoices. MASA: Can the TEMBIsA hospital, CEO perhaps claim ignorance? JEFF: That would be equally as damaging for him because this expenditure, according to our evidence, happened under his watch. So at best he's incompetent and at worst he's culpable. VO: While Dr. Mthunzi declined an interview, he was suspended alongside provincial CFO Lerato Madyo last week as the Special Investigation Unit moves forward with the case. A move that’s long overdue. JEFF: BABITA Deokaran did everything right// She picked up an anomaly. She reported it and she expected that something would be done. In fact, nothing was done and she was murdered. And that's the great tragedy of this story. VO: Seeing wrongdoing and looking the other way was never in Babita Deokaran’s nature. TONY: She died doing her job with integrity and diligently. She stood for the truth. And she would not Compromise. Our entire lives. Have been shaken and changed. We’ll never be the Same again. Because she is no more. So whilst we are. Paying the price as a family, the mastermind out there is still at large. VO: Arresting the alleged hitmen, is simply not good enough. ALEX: Another five can be hired for the next whistle blower. The end game for these hospitals in this investigation is that the key public sector people, people in public office responsible for this network, need to go to jail. VO: But that would be up to the authorities. JEFF: At the end of the day, we're journalists. We come into information, we verify it and we publish it. We're not the SIU or the police? And we're just making sure that everything that had been kept in the shadows is now in the light. END PROMOS PROMO 1 – 11 seconds A year after Whistleblower Babita Deokaran was gunned down, we retrace her steps in the days leading up to her murder and reveal the unbelievable level of graft she uncovered. PROMO 2 – 21 SECONDS VO: Whistleblower Babita Deokaran stood no chance - assassinated in a hit-style killing – she was silenced for speaking out. JEFF: This was her final graft investigation. VO: A year later a team of investigative journalists retrace her final steps, uncovering at least 850 million reasons for her to die. VO: Three weeks later she was murdered. TONY: She didn't tell us in detail what she was really involved in or what she really faced. // she stood for the truth. And she would not. Compromise.. M8 //

metadata.Summary: Babita Deokaran was a corruption whistle-blower within the Gauteng Department of Health. She was assassinated in a hit-style killing outside her south Johannesburg home in August 2021. Babita stood no chance. She put her life on the line when she chose to speak out and expose deep rooted corruption within the Gauteng Dept of Health. She knew it would be dangerous - but doing the right thing ended up costing her – her life. As a country we praise the whistleblowers as the pillars of truth and justice - Babita’s story is one that should shock and outrage the country – we cannot allow this failure of justice to be swept under rug. The Babita story has not been told in detail, the shocking elements that reveal a complete disregard for whistleblowers safety has never been more evident. I think her family would be open to speaking now and it could make for a compelling story retracing her steps in the days leading up to her murder. The masterminds behind her hit are still walking free and the orchestrators of the graft are still in their position and drawing salaries paid for by us tax payers! NEWS24 has done a remarkable 6 month long investigation – titled Silenced. We tell the story visually – the content is compelling and our reach will take the research to another level.
